plumbing.review:
Two findings need fixes:

- **[P2] Posts without closing instructions can change.** [comments.go:60](repo/internal/factory/comments.go:60) treats every backticked `/invariant …` reference as an instruction. For example, a long diagnostic ending with “The log contained `/invariant retry`.” now reserves that diagnostic and removes additional leading text. This can occur through [buildFailedComment](repo/internal/factory/comments.go:370), which includes error text but requests no command. It violates the promised unchanged output for posts without closing commands. The regression test uses only repeated `x` characters ([closing_commands_accept_test.go:165](repo/internal/factory/closing_commands_accept_test.go:165)), so misses this case.

- **[P2] Wrapped closing instructions lose their opening text.** [comments.go:66](repo/internal/factory/comments.go:66) starts preservation at the command’s line. An oversized body ending with `To ratify exactly this, comment\n` followed by the backticked ratify command loses “To ratify exactly this, comment”, even when the entire instruction fits. Preserve the complete instruction across line breaks. The multiple-line fixture places each complete instruction on its own line ([closing_commands_accept_test.go:132](repo/internal/factory/closing_commands_accept_test.go:132)), so does not catch this.

Otherwise, the diff stays within the approved file. Acceptance sources match the plan, exercise real clipping, and contain substantive assertions; there is no fixture-specific bypass. The factory reports all checks passing ([tests.txt:1](tests.txt:1)); I did not rerun Go tooling during this read-only review. The added code performs only string processing, introduces no host/network access or secret handling, and follows surrounding naming and comment style.

The documentation remains consistent; recording the two-way decision remains the merger’s responsibility ([plan.json:3](plan.json:3), [SPEC.md:96](repo/SPEC.md:96)).

VERDICT: changes needed — distinguish closing instructions from diagnostic references, preserve wrapped instructions completely, and add regression coverage for both.
